verdict.rationale: Unreal documents a public Remote Control API: an in-engine web server that handles HTTP requests and WebSocket messages through a REST-like API and can call any Blueprint-callable function. It also publishes a generated Unreal Python API reference for programmatically controlling the editor, so an agent has an official, documented programmatic surface. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agents drive the API reliably, a stable rather than Experimental-marked Python API reference, and documented control beyond operating from the same network.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Remote Control system makes this possible by running a web server inside the Unreal Engine that services WebSocket messages and HTTP requests made by remote web applications through a REST-like API.

You can call any function that is callable from Blueprint. This includes any function defined in C++ with the BlueprintCallable specifier, or any function that is defined and implemented entirely in Blueprint.
Control the Unreal Editor from UIs that you create yourself in Python.
the Python editor-scripting docs, Remote Control API references, and UAT/automation CLI docs on dev.epicgames.com/documentation ARE fetchable keylessly.
